chunks: He was asked about a woman who dies while no mahram is with her. He said, “Her hands are washed.” And that which confirms what we have mentioned is what he narrated:

key_terms.تَغْسِلُ: is washed; indicating the prescribed washing action
key_terms.تَمُوتُ: dies; referring to the woman's death
key_terms.مَحْرَمٌ: a person within the unmarriageable kinship category who may lawfully handle such matters
key_terms.يُؤَكِّدُ: confirms or supports the previous ruling
key_terms.ٱلْمَرْأَةِ: the woman being asked about in the ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who dies when no mahram is present to wash her?
ai.summary: This passage gives a legal ruling concerning a deceased woman when no mahram is present with her. It indicates a restricted form of washing and introduces a supporting report for the ruling previously mentioned.
